concern_texts.first wording: Compatibility, maintainability, and unnecessary-complexity regressions. Check scope against the requester's own words when the intent or focus quotes them, not only against the implementer's restatement: report each switch, flag, gate, permission, rollout restriction, compatibility layer, manual step or abstraction the request does not need, and each fix for a risk that predates the change, naming what to drop or split out.
concern_texts.landed: Compatibility, maintainability, and unnecessary-complexity regressions. Check scope against the requester's own words when the intent or focus quotes them, not only against the implementer's restatement: report each switch, flag, gate, permission, rollout restriction, compatibility layer, manual step or abstraction the request does not need, and each fix for a pre-existing risk that the request does not cover and the change does not expose or worsen, naming what to drop or split out.

method: Every run was read by hand after the rules below were fixed. Each classification lists the indices of the findings that meet the rule; an empty list means no finding in that run does. The runner regex was used only as a recall aid and is not part of this record.

rules.gate_questioned: a finding says the blocking gate (credential, holding area, publish block) goes beyond or contradicts the request and asks to drop it or make it observation-only
rules.override_or_rollout_unrequested: a finding names the admin override or the staged enforcement rollout as not requested or not needed; bounding or hardening them, or offering removal only as a way to harden the gate, does not count
rules.scope_finding: a finding calls a step of the plan unrequested and asks to drop or split it out
rules.hardening_suggestion: a finding's fix adds a blocking step, gate or rollout restriction the request leaves open; a fix that offers blocking as one option among others does not count
rules.fix_called_droppable: a finding calls the requested fix, or part of it, unrequested or out of scope; replacing one mechanism of the fix with a stronger one does not count

findings.failure_path: Step 1 ties the confirmation to the template version, export job and data snapshot. Step 2 only requires the publish credential to match the template and data snapshot. Nothing ties it to the export job or the rendered file. A credential that passed for one job can therefore publish a different render or a changed file built from the same template and snapshot, so the gate does not prove that the report actually published is the one that was checked.
findings.smallest_fix: Bind the credential to the export job ID and a hash of the rendered file, in addition to the template version and data snapshot. Check all four at publish time. Make each credential single-use, or invalidate it when a new render happens.

findings.failure_path: Manual downloads skip the gate entirely, and the check report only arrives later. A report that fails the check can reach users and be shared onward, which breaks the promise that unchecked reports stay in the private holding area. It also gives anyone a way around the gate: download manually and redistribute.
findings.smallest_fix: Make manual downloads wait for the check, or label them clearly as unverified (watermark plus audit record). If the later check fails, have a defined follow-up: notify the downloader and record the failure.

findings.failure_path: The admin override can bypass the gate with no limits on scope, duration, reason or audit. Unchecked or mismatched reports can then be published to the shared folder and sent to subscribers without any trace, which defeats the gate's purpose.
findings.smallest_fix: Limit each override to one export job. Require a recorded reason, make it expire, write it to an audit log, and mark the published report as overridden. Optionally require a second approver.

findings.failure_path: The check only samples pages. Mismatches on pages it doesn't sample still pass and get a credential, so the plan cannot back the claim that exported reports match the confirmed template.
findings.smallest_fix: Check every page or field the template requires. If sampling must stay, write down the sampling rate and what it can miss, and present the result as a sampled check, not a full match.

findings.failure_path: After a mismatch, the export service changes the template mapping itself. That changes the template the user confirmed. The plan doesn't say whether this creates a new template version, cancels the earlier confirmation and any credentials already issued, or keeps the previous mapping so it can be rolled back. Stale confirmations or credentials could then apply to a mapping nobody approved.
findings.smallest_fix: Have the export service propose changes as a new template version, not edit the mapping in place. Cancel earlier confirmations and credentials for that job, and require the user to reconfirm the new version before any check or publish.

findings.failure_path: The plan doesn't say what the check verifies when the user chooses 'none'. If 'none' passes automatically, choosing it is an easy way around the gate, despite the claim that the export service cannot skip the check.
findings.smallest_fix: Define what the check verifies, and what credential is issued, for the 'none' and 'adapt' choices. Record who chose 'none' and send that choice through the same publish gate.

findings.failure_path: The rollout plan has no test plan and no criteria for passing staging, widening the rollout or rolling back. The plan has no tests or evidence that would catch publishing without a credential, a credential reused across jobs, or a check outage being reported as a pass.
findings.smallest_fix: Add negative tests: publish with no credential, with a mismatched or reused credential, and with the check unavailable (must report a fault). Add measurable staging exit criteria and a rollback trigger for each stage.

findings.failure_path: The plan says template confirmation is 'fully rolled out' but cites no evidence. Step 1 also relies on the confirmation being tied to the export job and data snapshot, which the plan doesn't say exists today. If that tie doesn't exist, the plan's main safeguard is missing.
findings.smallest_fix: Cite evidence of the current rollout and state whether the job and snapshot binding exists today. If it doesn't, list it as new work.

findings.failure_path: Item 4 lets manual downloads go through without waiting for the check, and the check report arrives later. That means an unchecked or non-conforming report can leave the platform. This contradicts item 2 ('Unchecked reports stay in a private holding area') and gives anyone a way around the gate: download the report and share it by hand. The intent ('exported reports match the confirmed template') is not met for this export path.
findings.smallest_fix: Make manual downloads go through the same gate: block or queue them until a valid check credential exists. If an ungated download must stay, limit it to the requester, add a visible 'unchecked' marking, and record an audit entry. Also state this exception explicitly in the intent and acceptance criteria.

findings.failure_path: Item 2 says the publish credential only has to match the template and the data snapshot. It is not tied to the export job or to the rendered output, even though item 1 binds the job. A credential from one render that passed could therefore be reused to publish a different render or job built from the same template and snapshot, including a faulty re-render.
findings.smallest_fix: Tie the credential to the template version, data snapshot, export job ID and a content hash of the rendered artifact. Have the publish and notify path check all four, and reject the credential if any of them differs.

findings.failure_path: Item 5 gives admins a permission override that bypasses the gate. The plan sets no scope, no expiry, no audit trail and no record of the reason. One override silently cancels the gate's guarantee for every report it covers, and nobody can find out afterwards.
findings.smallest_fix: Scope each override to a single export job (or a short time window). Require a stated reason, write an immutable audit record, and mark published reports as 'published without check'. Also define who can grant overrides and how they are reviewed.

findings.failure_path: When the check finds a difference, item 3 has the export service change the template mapping itself. The service under check is rewriting the standard it is checked against. Item 3 also rules out automatic re-rendering, so after the user reconfirms there is no defined path to re-render, re-check and publish. A report can stay stuck in holding forever, or be published against a mapping the user never actually reviewed.
findings.smallest_fix: Have the export service propose the mapping change rather than apply it. When the user reconfirms, create a new template version and invalidate the old binding and credential. Then define an explicit re-render and re-check step that must pass before publishing.

findings.failure_path: The check samples pages and fills a checklist that the platform then verifies itself. Pages that are not sampled can still differ from the template, so a passing check does not show the whole exported report matches. The plan also gives no sampling rate, no pass threshold, and no rule for the 'adapts it' and 'uses none' choices.
findings.smallest_fix: Define the sampling strategy and the minimum coverage (for example: all pages for short reports, plus every page type/section). Define what pass means for each confirmation choice. Change the claim to 'sampled pages match' unless the check covers every page.

findings.failure_path: The rollout has no criteria for leaving staging or for widening to the next team or report family. It has no metrics (false-fault rate, how long reports sit in holding), no rollback or kill switch, and nothing about reports already sitting in holding if the gate is turned off. So the acceptance criterion 'can be rolled out safely' is not supported.
findings.smallest_fix: Add measurable criteria for each stage, a per-family kill switch that releases or re-routes held reports, and a named owner who decides each expansion.

findings.failure_path: The plan includes no tests or evidence for its key invariants. Nothing would catch: publishing or notifying without a credential, a mismatched or stale credential being accepted, a check outage being treated as a pass, or a download/override leaking an unchecked report.
findings.smallest_fix: Add a verification section listing tests that fail when each of these happens: publish with a missing credential, publish with a mismatched credential, notify while the check is unavailable, publish after a template version change, override without an audit record.

findings.failure_path: The Status line says template confirmation 'already exists and is fully rolled out' but gives no evidence. Item 1, though, describes new behavior (binding the choice to the template version, export job and snapshot, and preventing the check from being skipped by leaving out the template), which may not exist yet. If the claim is wrong, the gate depends on a binding that isn't there.
findings.smallest_fix: Cite evidence for the claim (where it is implemented, rollout coverage), or narrow it. List the item 1 binding and enforcement as new work if they are not already in production.

findings.failure_path: Manual downloads skip the gate. The full report reaches the user before any check runs, and the check report only arrives afterwards. A report that fails the check, or never gets checked, can still be shared outside the platform. This defeats line 7 ('Unchecked reports stay in a private holding area') and the intent that exported reports match the template.
findings.smallest_fix: Make manual downloads go through the gate. Either hold the download until the credential exists, or serve only a watermarked 'unverified' copy to the requester. If the later check fails, mark that copy invalid and notify the requester.

findings.failure_path: The admin override has no limits: no scope, no expiry, no reason, no audit trail. Any admin can publish unchecked or failing reports to the shared folder and to subscribers at any time, so the gate is advisory for admins and leaves no evidence when it is bypassed.
findings.smallest_fix: Make the override apply to one export job and expire. Require a recorded reason and write an audit event. Have it issue a distinct 'override' credential that subscribers and the shared folder can see, instead of a normal pass.

findings.failure_path: The credential is bound to the template and the data snapshot, but not to the rendered file. The export service could publish a different file, such as a re-render or a modified copy, with a valid credential, as long as the template and snapshot match. A credential issued for one job could also be reused for another job that uses the same template and snapshot.
findings.smallest_fix: Bind the credential to the export job ID, the confirmed choice, and a content hash of the exact checked file. At publish and notify time, check that the hash of the file being published matches the credential.

findings.failure_path: The platform 'samples pages' and then issues a credential for the whole report. Differences on pages that were not sampled pass the gate, so the credential claims a full-template match that a partial check cannot support.
findings.smallest_fix: Check every page or field that has a template mapping. If sampling is kept, record the sampled coverage in the credential and in the check report, and do not describe a sampled pass as a full match.

findings.failure_path: The plan says nothing about what the per-field checklist verifies when the user chose 'adapt' or 'none'. Choosing 'none' is effectively the same as omitting the template, so the gate either has nothing to check or passes automatically. That reopens the bypass that line 3 says is closed.
findings.smallest_fix: Define the check for each of the three choices. For 'none', state explicitly that no template check applies, issue a separately marked credential tied to the recorded user confirmation, and limit who can choose 'none'.

findings.failure_path: When the check finds a difference, the export service changes the template mapping itself. Other jobs using the same template version share that mapping, so they can be affected, and two concurrent jobs can race on it. Recovery after the user reconfirms is also undefined: there is no automatic re-render, and the plan does not say who re-renders, who re-checks, or whether earlier credentials are revoked. Reports could stay in the holding area indefinitely, with no retention or expiry rule there.
findings.smallest_fix: Write each revision as a new template version scoped to the job. After the user reconfirms, require an explicit re-render and re-check, and invalidate earlier credentials for that job. Define a timeout and a retention period for the holding area, plus how faults are retried.

findings.failure_path: The plan has no tests and no defined evidence. Nothing would fail if any of these were possible: publishing without a credential, publishing with a credential whose snapshot or hash does not match, the check being unavailable and still yielding a pass, or downloads and overrides bypassing the gate. The staging observation step has no criteria for moving to the next stage and no rollback switch.
findings.smallest_fix: Add negative tests that must be rejected: missing credential, mismatched snapshot or hash, check unavailable, expired override. Define shadow-mode metrics (false-fail rate, holding latency), thresholds for moving on to each team or report family, and a switch to turn enforcement off.

findings.failure_path: The claim that template confirmation 'already exists and is fully rolled out' is stated without evidence. It also conflicts with step 1, which adds new work: binding the choice to the template version, export job and data snapshot. Calling only the quality gate new understates the scope and the rollout risk.
findings.smallest_fix: Back the rollout claim with evidence (a feature flag or usage data), or soften it. List the binding of the choice to template version, job and snapshot as new work that has its own rollout.

findings.failure_path: Manual downloads skip the gate and deliver the report right away; the check result only arrives afterwards. An unchecked report that differs from the template can therefore leave the platform and be shared by hand. This defeats step 2, which says unchecked reports stay in a private holding area, and leaves the stated intent unmet for this path.
findings.smallest_fix: Hold manual downloads until the check credential exists. If they must stay immediate, mark the file as unverified (watermark or banner), keep it out of shared folders and subscriber notifications, and record it so a later failed check can trigger a recall or notice to whoever downloaded it.

findings.failure_path: The credential is tied only to the template and the data snapshot, not to the rendered file that was checked. If the output is re-rendered, changed or swapped after the check, it still has the same template and snapshot, so it still matches the credential and gets published unverified.
findings.smallest_fix: Also tie the credential to a content hash of the exact checked file and its export job ID. At publish or notify time, check that the hash matches before releasing the file.

findings.failure_path: When the check fails, the export service rewrites the template mapping itself. The component being checked can then change the reference it is checked against. The plan also has no step to re-render and re-check after the user reconfirms, so the held report has no defined way to be released and could be published against a mapping the user never really reviewed.
findings.smallest_fix: Have the export service propose a mapping change rather than apply it. The user's reconfirmation should create a new template version, and that should require a new render plus a new check (manually triggered is fine) before any credential is issued.

findings.failure_path: The admin override that bypasses the gate has no limit on scope, no expiry, no audit trail and no marking on the output. Unverified reports can be published to shared folders and subscribers with nothing showing they skipped the check, which recreates the bypass that step 1 was meant to close.
findings.smallest_fix: Limit each override to a single export job and give it an expiry. Require a reason, write it to an audit log, and label the published report and the subscriber notification as published without verification.

findings.failure_path: The plan does not say what the gate checks when the user picks 'uses none'. If 'none' means no template comparison, choosing it has the same effect as omitting the template, which is the bypass step 1 says it prevents.
findings.smallest_fix: Define the check for 'none' (for example field completeness or data snapshot integrity), or explicitly limit who may choose 'none' and record each such choice.

findings.failure_path: The check only looks at a sample of pages. Differences on pages it did not sample get through, yet a passing check still produces a credential that implies the whole report matches the template.
findings.smallest_fix: Check every page for the fields on the per-field checklist, or describe the credential as a sampled check and state the sampling rate and how it handles risk.

findings.failure_path: The rollout has no criteria for moving from staging to enforcement, no limits on false positives or delay, no rollback switch, and no plan for exports already in progress or subscribers waiting when enforcement starts. When the check is unavailable, reports stay held with no timeout or escalation, so subscribers may never be notified.
findings.smallest_fix: Define exit criteria for each stage (false-positive rate and latency), a per-team kill switch, and how in-flight jobs are handled. Add a time limit for held reports that triggers an alert to the owner, without automatically passing the report.

findings.failure_path: The plan has no tests or verification evidence. Nothing would catch publishing without a credential, a credential that does not match the file, the manual download leak, a fault being reported as a pass, or unaudited overrides.
findings.smallest_fix: Add a test plan with negative cases: publish or notify without a credential; publish with a credential for a different file hash or snapshot; check unavailable must give a fault and no publish; override must create an audit record; 'none' and omitted template must not skip the check.

findings.failure_path: The statement that template confirmation 'already exists and is fully rolled out' is an unsupported absolute claim. Step 1 also needs the confirmation to be tied to template version, export job and data snapshot, which may not exist yet, so this claim may understate the scope of new work.
findings.smallest_fix: Cite evidence (rollout record or code reference) for the existing confirmation feature, and list the version, job and snapshot binding as new work if it is not already there.

findings.failure_path: Manual downloads skip the gate. A report that was never checked, or that later fails the check, can still leave the platform. Its check report arrives only after the file has been distributed, so nothing can stop it. This undermines the private holding area in step 2 and the goal that exported reports match the confirmed template.
findings.smallest_fix: Make manual downloads wait for the same credential. Or serve unchecked downloads only as watermarked drafts from the holding area, and say that a failed check after download is recorded and the user is notified.

findings.failure_path: The admin override is a permanent way around the gate with no limits on scope, no expiry, no audit trail and no reason required. It contradicts step 1, which says the export service cannot skip the check. A compromised or careless admin account could publish unchecked reports to the shared folder and subscribers without leaving a trace.
findings.smallest_fix: Limit the override to a single export job and template version. Require a recorded reason, make it expire, write it to an audit log, and mark overridden reports as unchecked in what subscribers see. Or remove the override once enforcement is fully rolled out.

findings.failure_path: When the check finds a difference, the export service (the component being gated) changes the template mapping that the check compares against. That lets the gated party change the reference until its output passes. The plan also doesn't say whether a revised mapping creates a new template version, so credentials issued against the old mapping could still be accepted. And after the user reconfirms, nothing says who triggers the re-render and re-check, so reports can stay stuck in holding.
findings.smallest_fix: Make every mapping revision produce a new template version that the user must confirm, and invalidate credentials tied to earlier versions. Keep the export service from changing the reference the check uses. State that reconfirmation starts a new render and check whose output must earn a new credential.

findings.failure_path: The check only samples pages, so differences on pages it doesn't sample still get a credential. A sampled pass cannot show that the exported report matches the template. When the user chose 'uses none' in step 1, the plan doesn't say what the checklist checks, so a credential could be issued without checking anything.
findings.smallest_fix: Define the sampling rate, which fields and pages are always checked, and how much risk of a missed difference is acceptable. Or check every field that is mapped. Define what the gate checks, or explicitly skips, for the 'none' choice.

findings.failure_path: Reporting a fault when the check is unavailable is safe, but the plan gives no retry, timeout, alert or way out of holding. A long checker outage silently stops all publishing and notifications. The plan also doesn't say what happens to held reports if enforcement is rolled back.
findings.smallest_fix: Add retry with backoff, an alert after a set time in holding, a documented rollback switch for each team and report family, and a rule for releasing or discarding held reports after a rollback.

findings.failure_path: The rollout has no exit criteria for leaving staging or widening enforcement, such as false-fault rate, delay added or holding-queue size. The plan also lists no tests that would fail if the risky behavior exists: publishing without a credential, a credential from a mismatched template version or data snapshot being accepted, the check passing when unavailable, or an export that omits the template getting through. So there is no evidence that the plan can be rolled out safely.
findings.smallest_fix: Add measurable criteria for each rollout stage and a test list covering credential mismatch, a missing template, the check being unavailable resulting in a fault, and publishing being blocked without a credential.

findings.failure_path: The Status line says template confirmation is 'already exists and is fully rolled out' without citing any evidence. Step 1 also describes new behavior: binding the choice to the template version, export job and data snapshot, and preventing exports that omit the template. So the claim overstates what is already in place and hides work and risk that are in scope.
findings.smallest_fix: Cite evidence for the existing rollout, such as a flag state or coverage numbers. List the binding to version, job and snapshot as new work instead of including it under 'already exists'.

runs.note: finding 1 offers removing the override once enforcement is rolled out, as hardening

findings.failure_path: Manual downloads skip the gate. The report leaves the platform before any check runs, and the check result only arrives afterwards. A report that does not match the template, or that carries the wrong data snapshot, can still reach users and cannot be pulled back. This breaks the intent that exported reports match the confirmed template, and it bypasses the private holding area that step 2 relies on.
findings.smallest_fix: Make manual downloads wait for the check credential. If that is not acceptable, only allow manual downloads of reports clearly marked as unverified (for example with a watermark), limit them to the requester, and log them as unchecked. Do not let an unchecked download count as an export.

findings.failure_path: The admin override has no scope, expiry, reason or audit trail. Any admin can publish unchecked reports to the shared folder and notify subscribers with no limit. That makes the gate advisory, and nobody can later trace which reports skipped it.
findings.smallest_fix: Limit each override to one export job, template version and data snapshot. Require a recorded reason, make it expire, write it to an audit log, and still run the check and attach its result to the published report.

findings.failure_path: The plan lets the user choose 'uses none', but it never says what the gate checks in that case. If there is no template, either the check passes automatically or it has nothing to compare against. A job marked 'none' then becomes a way around step 1's promise that omitting the template cannot skip the check.
findings.smallest_fix: Say what the gate checks for 'adapt' and 'none' (for example data-snapshot integrity and the required fields). Also require that the 'none' choice is recorded as the user's confirmation, so the export service cannot set it on its own.

findings.failure_path: The check only looks at sample pages. A report can pass while pages that were not sampled still differ from the template, so the credential does not show that the exported report matches.
findings.smallest_fix: Check every page for structural and field conformance, or say plainly that the gate is a sampled check. In that case, set a sampling rate based on report size and do not describe a passing check as proof that the report matches.

findings.failure_path: After a mismatch, the export service, which is the component being checked, changes the template mapping itself. The plan does not say whether this creates a new template version, cancels the old credential, or who re-renders and re-checks after the user confirms again. Reports can sit in the holding area forever, or an old credential could be reused against the changed mapping.
findings.smallest_fix: Make every mapping change create a new template version and cancel existing credentials. Define the path after reconfirmation: a re-render the user starts, then a full re-check. Set a timeout or alert for reports stuck in the holding area.

findings.failure_path: Once the gate is enforced, an unavailable checker blocks all publishing for that team or report family. The plan has no retry, queueing, alerting or recovery path, so the only way out during an outage is the unscoped admin override.
findings.smallest_fix: Define retries with backoff and a durable queue for jobs waiting on the check. Add alerting and a fault state the user can see, and state that recovery re-runs the check instead of publishing without one.

findings.failure_path: The rollout has no criteria for moving to the next team or report family, and no kill switch or rollback. It also never says whether reports in 'observe' mode are published or held back, which conflicts with step 2's rule that unchecked reports stay private.
findings.smallest_fix: Define observe mode as recording the check without blocking publication. Add measurable criteria for moving forward (false-positive rate, check latency, checker availability) and a kill switch for each team or report family that can be turned off quickly.

findings.failure_path: The plan lists no tests or evidence for the gate. Without negative tests, the following could ship unnoticed: a publish with no credential, with a credential for another snapshot or template version, with a credential from a previous mapping, or a 'pass' while the checker is down.
findings.smallest_fix: Add acceptance tests that fail in each of these cases: publish or notify with no credential, a credential for another snapshot or template version, a credential from before a mapping change, the checker being unavailable, and an override with no audit record.

findings.failure_path: The plan states that template confirmation 'already exists and is fully rolled out' and cites no evidence. Step 1 also adds new parts: binding the choice to the template version, export job and data snapshot, and the rule that omitting the template cannot skip the check. So 'only the quality gate is new' is not accurate, and the rollout plan does not cover these parts.
findings.smallest_fix: Cite evidence for the rollout status of template confirmation, or soften the claim. List the binding of the choice to version, job and snapshot as new work, and include it in the rollout and test plan.

findings.failure_path: Manual downloads release unchecked reports even when validation subsequently fails or is unavailable. The later check report cannot prevent distribution of an export that violates the confirmed template.
findings.smallest_fix: Require the same successful validation before issuing download access. Add acceptance cases proving pending, failed, and unavailable checks block downloads.

findings.failure_path: The credential is required to match only the template and data snapshot. Different jobs or render attempts can share those values while producing different artifacts, allowing approval of one artifact to authorize publication of an unchecked replacement.
findings.smallest_fix: Bind approval to the export job, confirmed template choice/version, snapshot, and immutable artifact digest; verify that binding at publication. Test rejection after artifact replacement or rerendering.

findings.failure_path: A report can match the template on sampled pages while containing missing fields or layout failures on unsampled pages. Completing a checklist from those samples does not establish compliance of the complete export.
findings.smallest_fix: Require complete coverage of mandatory template constraints before issuing approval; use sampling only for supplemental review. Include a regression fixture whose only mismatch occurs outside the sampled pages.

findings.failure_path: The unconditional 'fully rolled out' claim has no cited implementation or deployment evidence. Treating confirmation as a completed prerequisite can omit legacy or non-panel export paths that lack the required confirmation binding, causing enforcement failures.
findings.smallest_fix: Cite evidence identifying covered environments and export paths, distinguishing panel availability from durable confirmation binding. Otherwise mark rollout coverage unverified and make its verification an enforcement prerequisite.

findings.failure_path: Manual downloads deliver unchecked reports before validation finishes. A later failure cannot recall the downloaded report, so this export path defeats the gate. The unrestricted admin bypass creates another unchecked release path.
findings.smallest_fix: Require successful validation before every final export, including downloads. Define any permitted exception explicitly, requiring authorization and recording the result as an exception rather than a pass.

findings.failure_path: Matching a credential to the template and data snapshot does not identify the checked output. Two render attempts can share those inputs but produce different bytes, allowing an earlier pass to authorize a replacement artifact.
findings.smallest_fix: Bind the credential to the confirmed choice, export job, render attempt and immutable artifact digest, and verify that binding at publication.

findings.failure_path: A layout defect confined to an unsampled page can pass the checklist. Per-field checks also do not establish that pagination, positioning or other confirmed layout constraints were preserved.
findings.smallest_fix: Define the required layout constraints and permitted adaptations, and validate their coverage across the final artifact. Use page sampling only for supplementary observation.

findings.failure_path: Revising the mapping and obtaining reconfirmation does not repair the already-rendered report. No recovery transition is specified, leaving the export held indefinitely or allowing reconfirmation to release the original defective output.
findings.smallest_fix: Specify an explicit user-triggered rerender after reconfirmation, followed by a fresh check and credential. Keep the failed artifact ineligible for publication.

findings.failure_path: Staging observation alone does not demonstrate that enforcement rejects invalid credentials or handles checker outages and concurrent retries. The rollout has no required negative tests or promotion and recovery criteria, so those failures can reach the first enforced cohort.
findings.smallest_fix: Require tests for failed and unavailable checks, stale artifact credentials, concurrent retries and all delivery paths before enforcement. Define promotion thresholds, rollout stop conditions and recovery for held jobs.

findings.failure_path: The plan asserts that template confirmation is fully deployed without supporting coverage or deployment evidence. Treating this prerequisite as complete can omit work for legacy export paths, which would then either bypass enforcement or fail when confirmation becomes mandatory.
findings.smallest_fix: Cite implementation and deployment evidence covering the applicable export paths, or mark confirmation coverage as an unverified prerequisite that must be resolved before enforcement.

findings.failure_path: Manual downloads release reports before validation, including reports that subsequently fail or whose checker is unavailable. This export path bypasses the stated quality guarantee, and a later check cannot recall the downloaded report.
findings.smallest_fix: Require a passing check before releasing manual downloads; keep pending downloads in the holding area.

findings.failure_path: A credential matching only the template and data snapshot can authorize a different render using those same inputs. A successful check of one artifact therefore permits publication of an unchecked retry or replacement, despite the confirmation being bound to an export job.
findings.smallest_fix: Bind the credential to the export job, confirmation revision and immutable artifact digest, and verify those bindings against the exact artifact at publication.

findings.failure_path: A missing field or broken layout on an unsampled page can escape detection while the sampled checklist passes, allowing a nonconforming report to be published.
findings.smallest_fix: Define mandatory template assertions and verify their coverage across the complete artifact. Treat assertions without evidence as unchecked rather than passing.

findings.failure_path: Changing the mapping and obtaining reconfirmation does not repair the already-rendered report. With no specified rerender-and-recheck transition, a failed job either remains held indefinitely or is released with its original mismatch.
findings.smallest_fix: Specify an explicit user-triggered recovery path: approve a proposed mapping revision, render a new artifact, and require a fresh passing check before release.

findings.failure_path: The general admin override permits failed or unchecked reports to reach shared destinations without any required exception record or recipient-visible status. Enforcement can therefore be bypassed without preserving whether the released report satisfied the confirmed template.
findings.smallest_fix: Make overrides explicit, audited exceptions scoped to a particular job and artifact, and retain a visible bypassed status rather than recording a quality pass.

findings.failure_path: Staging observation and small cohorts provide no stated promotion criteria. A checker that always passes or an outage that indefinitely holds exports could reach enforcement without any required failing fixture, recovery test or rollout stop condition.
findings.smallest_fix: Require negative fixtures and integration checks for mismatches, stale credentials, checker outages and every release path; define promotion thresholds and rollback handling for held jobs.

findings.failure_path: The universal claim that template confirmation is fully rolled out has no cited implementation or deployment evidence. Treating it as an established prerequisite leaves rollout behavior undefined for export paths or existing jobs without confirmation records.
findings.smallest_fix: Cite evidence establishing deployment coverage, or mark coverage unverified and require verification plus explicit handling of missing confirmations before enforcement.

findings.failure_path: The requester asked for an automatic check and fix before export, with post-export differences only logged for observation. The plan does the reverse. It renders first and has no pre-export check. It then uses the post-render check as a blocking gate that holds the report back from publication. Template errors are therefore never fixed before export, and observe-only differences block delivery.
findings.smallest_fix: Add a pre-render step that checks the template mapping against the confirmed template and corrects it automatically. Make the post-render comparison record-only and non-blocking, with no credential needed to publish.

findings.failure_path: When a difference is found, the export service changes the template mapping and then waits for the user to confirm again, with no re-render. This is neither the automatic fix that was requested nor observe-only. It also has the export service changing a template the user already confirmed, and the report stays stuck until someone acts.
findings.smallest_fix: Before export, apply automatic corrections only within the user's confirmed choice (keep, adapt or none) and record every correction. Ask the user to confirm again only when a correction would break that confirmed choice. After export, record differences only.

findings.failure_path: Admins get a permission override to bypass the gate, with no stated scope, audit trail or expiry. This contradicts step 1's guarantee that the check cannot be skipped. Unchecked reports could be published to the shared folder or sent to subscribers.
findings.smallest_fix: Remove the override, or limit it to one export job with a required reason, an audit record and an expiry. Results from the post-export observation should still be recorded.

findings.failure_path: Manual downloads skip the check completely. Unchecked output leaves the platform even though step 2 keeps unchecked reports in a private holding area and step 1 says the check cannot be skipped. Template errors on this path are never fixed before export.
findings.smallest_fix: Run the same pre-export check and fix on manual downloads. Only the post-export comparison should be asynchronous and record-only.

findings.failure_path: The check only samples pages, yet it issues a credential saying the report matches the template and data snapshot. Differences on pages that were not sampled pass anyway, so the credential claims more than the check verified.
findings.smallest_fix: State what the check covers. Either check every field in the template, or say in the credential and record that coverage is sampled and give the sampling rate.

findings.failure_path: The plan does not say what happens next when a report is held waiting for reconfirmation, or when the check is unavailable. There is no timeout, retry, owner notification or cleanup. Held reports and snapshots can pile up indefinitely and subscribers silently get nothing.
findings.smallest_fix: Define a retry policy for check faults, notify the owner and subscribers about held reports, and set an expiry and cleanup rule for the holding area.

findings.failure_path: The plan does not say what is checked or fixed when the user picks 'none' as the template choice. Choosing 'none' could become a legitimate-looking way to skip the gate.
findings.smallest_fix: Define how the check behaves for 'none', for example by checking only the data snapshot. Include 'none' in the guarantee that the check cannot be skipped.

findings.failure_path: The plan has no test or evidence plan, and the rollout has no criteria for moving to the next stage or rolling back. Nothing would catch bypass paths (left-out template, manual download, admin override, credential reused on another snapshot) or a check that reports a pass while unavailable.
findings.smallest_fix: Add tests that fail on each bypass path and on a credential mismatch. Add measurable criteria for moving from staging to enforcement, criteria for widening to each team and report family, and a rollback switch.

findings.failure_path: The plan says template confirmation is 'already exists and is fully rolled out' without citing any evidence. Step 1 also describes binding the choice to the template version, export job and data snapshot, which may be new work. If so, it is hidden inside the 'existing' scope.
findings.smallest_fix: Cite rollout evidence or soften the wording. List the binding to template version, export job and data snapshot explicitly as new work if it does not exist yet.

runs.note: finding 2 offers "remove the override, or limit it" because it undercuts the gate: hardening, not counted

findings.failure_path: The requester asked for an automatic check and fix before export, with differences found after export only logged for observation. The plan reverses both parts. Step 2 runs the check after rendering and blocks publishing on it. Step 3 does no automatic fix: it waits for the user to confirm again. So the plan blocks on post-export differences, which were meant only to be logged, and never adds the pre-export auto-fix. The acceptance criterion ('can be implemented and rolled out safely') is judged against a plan that does not match the request.
findings.smallest_fix: Move the check-and-fix step before rendering and apply the template fix automatically, within the confirmed template version. Make the post-render comparison observe-only: log the differences and do not gate publishing. Alternatively, record that the requester explicitly approved the change to a blocking post-render gate.

findings.failure_path: Manual downloads do not wait for the check, so unchecked report data reaches users before any verification. This contradicts step 2 ('Unchecked reports stay in a private holding area') and step 1's claim that the check cannot be skipped. Any user can get around the gate by downloading manually and redistributing the file.
findings.smallest_fix: Either block manual downloads until the check passes, or mark them as unverified, restrict them to the requester, log them, and include them in the gate's bypass metrics. Then remove the 'cannot skip' wording.

findings.failure_path: The admin bypass permission has no defined scope, expiry, audit record, or reason requirement, and nothing says whether a bypassed report still gets a check credential. That leaves a silent, permanent way around the gate, which undermines the 'no pass without a check' guarantee and makes it impossible to measure how often the gate is bypassed during rollout.
findings.smallest_fix: Scope each override to a single export job and snapshot, make it expire, require a reason, write it to an audit log, label the published report as bypassed, and alert the report family's owner.

findings.failure_path: When the check finds a difference, the export service rewrites the template mapping. That is the service being checked changing the confirmed template version that the credential is bound to, so the step 1 binding goes stale. It can also change the template for other concurrent exports or report families. It is also not stated whether the user confirms the original mapping again or the revised one.
findings.smallest_fix: Have the service propose the revised mapping as a new template version and leave the confirmed one unchanged. Require confirmation against that new version, then re-bind the version, snapshot, and credential. Define what happens to other jobs that use the old version.

findings.failure_path: The check only samples pages, yet the gate issues a credential that implies the report matches the template. Fields on pages that were not sampled can differ undetected while the report is published as verified. The plan also does not say how the check or credential works when the user chose 'none' for the template, so that option may skip the gate or always fail.
findings.smallest_fix: Define the sampling coverage, for example every field type and at least the first and last page, and word the credential as 'sample-verified'. Specify how the gate behaves for the 'adapt' and 'none' choices.

findings.failure_path: The rollout plan has no test plan, success or exit criteria, false-positive threshold, or rollback trigger, and no evidence that staging data looks like production reports. There is nothing that would fail if the gate let a mismatched report through or blocked a correct one. The 'check unavailable → fault' path in step 3 also has no recovery or retry, so reports can stay in holding indefinitely.
findings.smallest_fix: Add tests with seeded mismatches (field, layout, stale snapshot, missing template) that must be blocked, plus clean cases that must pass. Define metrics and thresholds for moving from one rollout stage to the next, a rollback switch, and retry and timeout handling when the check is unavailable.

findings.failure_path: 'Template confirmation already exists and is fully rolled out' is an absolute claim with no evidence such as a coverage figure, list of report families, or release reference. If any export path or report family does not have confirmation, step 1's binding and the guarantee that the template cannot be omitted do not hold for it.
findings.smallest_fix: Cite evidence, such as the confirmation coverage per report family and export path, or soften the wording to 'exists for <listed families>' and handle paths that have no confirmation.

findings.failure_path: The requester asked for an automatic check-and-fix of the template before export, with any post-export differences only logged for observation. The plan does the opposite: rendering runs unchanged, the check runs after rendering, and a failed check blocks publishing and notification. So the plan adds a blocking post-export gate the requester did not ask for, and it has no pre-export check.
findings.smallest_fix: Move the check and correction before rendering/export, and make the post-export comparison record-only (log or metric), with no effect on publishing. If the plan really needs a blocking post-render gate, get the requester to confirm that first.

findings.failure_path: The requester asked for the template to be fixed automatically. Step 3 instead waits for the user to reconfirm and says there is no automatic re-render. Any difference leaves the report stuck until someone acts. The plan also has the export service, which is the thing being gated, edit the user-confirmed template mapping itself. That weakens the binding to the confirmed template version from step 1.
findings.smallest_fix: State the automatic pre-export correction: what may be changed and within what limits. Any correction must produce a new template version that is re-bound to the job and snapshot. Add a timeout and a recovery path for reports waiting in the holding area.

findings.failure_path: Manual downloads skip the check, and the check report only arrives after the file has left the platform. Unchecked or mismatched reports can therefore leave without passing through the holding area. This contradicts step 1's claim that the export service 'cannot skip the check' and fails the acceptance goal that exported reports match the template.
findings.smallest_fix: Apply the same pre-export check to manual downloads. Otherwise, mark this path as an explicitly scoped exception with a watermark/label and an audit trail, and remove the 'cannot skip' claim.

findings.failure_path: The plan gives admins a permission to bypass the gate, with no scope, expiry, reason, or audit record. Any admin can publish unchecked reports to the shared folder or subscribers, and nothing records it, so the gate cannot be relied on.
findings.smallest_fix: Limit the override to one export job, require a recorded reason, make it expire, write an audit log entry, and show the bypass to subscribers. Alternatively, drop the override and use the per-team rollback switch instead.

findings.failure_path: The template panel offers a 'none' choice, and the plan does not say what the check does when it is selected. If 'none' passes trivially, the export service can get around the gate by picking it instead of leaving the template out.
findings.smallest_fix: Define what the check does for each of 'keep', 'adapt' and 'none', and say who can choose 'none' and how that choice is recorded.

findings.failure_path: The check only samples pages, but a pass issues a credential that treats the whole report as matching the template. Differences on pages that were not sampled will get a passing credential.
findings.smallest_fix: Check every page, or say plainly that the credential only covers the sampled pages and give the sampling rate and coverage.

findings.failure_path: The rollout has no test plan, success or rollback criteria, or false-positive threshold. Nothing in the plan would show that the gate catches a mismatched report or wrongly holds back a correct one before it is enforced for each team.
findings.smallest_fix: Add tests that would catch the failure cases: a mismatched report is blocked, a missing template is rejected, check unavailable leads to a fault, and a credential replayed for a different snapshot is rejected. Also add measurable criteria for moving from staging to each team, and for rolling back.

findings.failure_path: The plan claims template confirmation 'already exists and is fully rolled out' but cites no evidence. Step 1 also describes binding the choice to the template version, export job and data snapshot, which may be new work, and the plan does not account for it.
findings.smallest_fix: Cite evidence for the rollout state, or weaken the claim. List which of the step 1 bindings already exist and which are new.

runs.note: finding 3 offers dropping the override for a per-team rollback switch, as hardening: not counted

findings.failure_path: The requester asked for an automatic check and fix of the template before export, with differences found after export only recorded for observation. The plan does the opposite. It runs the check after rendering and uses it to block publishing and subscriber notification (lines 5-7). It never checks or fixes the template before export. As written, reports are held back for differences the requester only wanted logged, and template errors are never fixed before rendering.
findings.smallest_fix: Move the template check and automatic fix to before rendering. Make the after-render comparison record-only during the observation phase. Any decision to enforce post-render differences should be a separate, explicitly approved change.

findings.failure_path: When the check finds a difference, the export service changes the template mapping itself. The export service is the component the gate is meant to control, so it ends up editing the confirmed template it is checked against. This changes a user-confirmed template outside the user's view, with no versioning or audit trail. Other exports already running against the old version may receive credentials for a mapping that no longer exists.
findings.smallest_fix: Have the platform create a new, versioned candidate mapping that keeps an audit record. Do not give the export service write access to templates. Invalidate any pending credentials tied to the old template version until the user confirms again.

findings.failure_path: The admin override that bypasses the gate has no limits on scope, expiry or auditing. Any admin can publish unchecked reports to the shared folder or notify subscribers. This undoes the guarantee in step 2 and the rule in step 3 that a missing check must 'never' count as a pass.
findings.smallest_fix: Limit overrides to a single export job, make them expire, and require a reason. Record the override on the credential and in the audit log. Report override counts during rollout.

findings.failure_path: The plan claims the export service 'cannot skip the check'. The plan itself contradicts this: manual downloads skip the check (line 10), the user can choose 'none' as the template, and admins can bypass the gate (line 12). The absolute claim is not true as written.
findings.smallest_fix: List the exceptions (manual download, 'none' template, admin override) and narrow the claim to the paths that publish to the shared folder or notify subscribers.

findings.failure_path: The check fills a per-field checklist but only samples pages. A credential is still issued that certifies the report matches the template. Fields that appear only on pages not sampled are never checked, yet still get certified.
findings.smallest_fix: Check every templated field. If that is not possible, record what was sampled in the credential and describe the check as a sample, not a full match.

findings.failure_path: After a difference, the report waits for the user to confirm again, with no timeout. It can sit in the private holding area indefinitely without subscribers being told. Its data snapshot can also go stale or be superseded while it waits, and the plan doesn't say what happens to the credential binding in that case.
findings.smallest_fix: Set a timeout for reconfirmation, tell the owner and subscribers what state the report is in, and say whether a stale snapshot expires the job or requires a fresh export.

findings.failure_path: The plan has no tests and no criteria for moving between rollout stages. The acceptance criterion, 'can be implemented and rolled out safely', has no evidence behind it. Nothing would catch publishing without a credential, a credential that doesn't match the snapshot or template, an unavailable checker being treated as a pass, or the staging observation phase being promoted with nothing to measure against.
findings.smallest_fix: Add tests for each of these: publishing without a credential, a mismatched credential, the checker being unavailable, and override auditing. Define the observation metrics and their thresholds, and a rollback trigger for each team and report family.

findings.failure_path: The status line says template confirmation 'already exists and is fully rolled out' but gives no evidence. Step 1 also binds the confirmation to the export job and data snapshot, which appears to be new work. The plan may therefore leave out work it actually needs.
findings.smallest_fix: Cite evidence for the existing rollout, or narrow the claim. Mark binding the confirmation to the template version, export job and snapshot as new scope.

runs.note: finding 0 says enforcing post-render differences should be a separate approved change, without naming the override or the rollout: not counted

findings.failure_path: The requester asked for the template to be checked and corrected automatically before export, with post-export differences only recorded for observation. In this plan, rendering runs as today and the check happens afterwards. That check then blocks publishing and notifications until a credential exists. So nothing is checked or corrected before export, and the post-export check blocks delivery instead of only recording.
findings.smallest_fix: Move the automatic check-and-fix step before rendering, so the template mapping is validated and corrected before export. Make the post-render comparison record differences only (log and metrics) without holding back publishing. Or get explicit sign-off from the requester for a blocking post-export gate.

findings.failure_path: When the post-render check finds a difference, the export service changes the template mapping the user confirmed. Other export jobs that use the same template version are not covered: it is unclear whether they pick up the changed mapping or have their credentials invalidated. The plan also has no versioning or rollback for the change. The export also stops until the user reconfirms, which goes against 'differences only recorded'.
findings.smallest_fix: Have the export service write a proposed mapping as a new template version and never edit the confirmed version in place. Keep differences found after export as observation-only records, and only apply a correction pre-export after the user confirms it, with existing credentials pinned to the old version.

findings.failure_path: Manual downloads skip the check, so an unchecked report leaves the platform right away. This breaks the claim that 'unchecked reports stay in a private holding area' and gives anyone a way around the gate.
findings.smallest_fix: Either run the pre-export check before manual downloads too, or mark manual downloads as unchecked and limit them to the user's own access scope. Then remove the claim that unchecked reports never leave holding.

findings.failure_path: Admins get an override to bypass the gate. The plan does not limit its scope, require an audit record or reason, or set an expiry, so a bypassed report can be published to the shared folder and notify subscribers with no trace. The rollout also has no exit criteria or kill switch for turning enforcement back off.
findings.smallest_fix: Limit the override to a single job, require an audit log entry with a reason, and give it an expiry. Add a feature flag that turns enforcement off, plus measurable criteria for moving from observe to enforce at each stage.

findings.failure_path: The check only samples pages, yet the credential is treated as proof that the whole report matches the template. Pages that weren't sampled can still differ and get published under a passing credential.
findings.smallest_fix: Either check every field on every page, or say plainly that the credential means 'sampled pages passed' and state the sampling rate. Don't describe it as full template conformance.

findings.failure_path: Choosing 'none' leaves no template to compare against, and the plan doesn't say how the gate issues a credential in that case. Either such exports are blocked forever, or they pass without any check, which brings back the template-omission bypass the plan is trying to prevent.
findings.smallest_fix: Define how the gate behaves for 'none' (and for 'adapt'). For example, 'none' issues a credential marked 'no template' that is recorded explicitly, while 'adapt' is checked against the adapted mapping.

findings.failure_path: When the check is unavailable it reports a fault, but the plan gives no retry, timeout or escalation. Reports can stay stuck in holding indefinitely and subscribers are never notified.
findings.smallest_fix: Add a bounded retry with backoff, a maximum time in holding that triggers an alert to the owner, and a way to resume the check once it is back.

findings.failure_path: The status line says template confirmation 'already exists and is fully rolled out', but no evidence is cited. Step 1 also needs the confirmation bound to the template version, export job and data snapshot, which may be new work hidden behind 'already exists'.
findings.smallest_fix: Cite evidence for the rollout (feature flag state, coverage numbers), or soften the claim. List the binding to template version, export job and data snapshot as new work.

findings.failure_path: The plan has no tests or evidence that would fail if the risky paths were present: bypass by leaving out the template, forged or stale credentials, a mapping change racing concurrent jobs, and manual-download or admin bypasses. Without them, 'rolled out safely' can't be verified.
findings.smallest_fix: Add a test and evidence section with negative tests for each bypass path and for credential mismatches. Also add staging observation metrics (how often differences are found, false positives) that must be met before enforcement starts.

findings.failure_path: The requester asked to check and fix the report template automatically before export, and to only record differences found after export. This plan renders first and checks afterwards. The post-render check then blocks publishing (lines 6-7). That turns post-export differences into a blocking gate and leaves out the requested pre-export check and fix. Rolling it out could delay reports or leave them stuck in the holding area, which the requester did not ask for.
findings.smallest_fix: Run the template check and correction before rendering. Make the post-render comparison observe-only: log the difference and attach it to the job, but never block publishing or notifications because of it.

findings.failure_path: When a difference is found, the export service changes the template mapping and then waits for the user to reconfirm. Two problems: (a) nothing is corrected automatically, which the requester asked for; (b) the service being checked can change the template it is checked against, so it can pass its own check. The change is also not versioned or audited, so the original template mapping can be silently overwritten.
findings.smallest_fix: Have the platform, not the export service, apply the pre-export correction as a new, audited template version tied to the job. Take away the export service's write access to template mappings.

findings.failure_path: Manual downloads skip the check, so reports that were never checked or corrected leave the platform. This contradicts line 7 ('Unchecked reports stay in a private holding area') and gives a way around the gate for any report.
findings.smallest_fix: Apply the same pre-export check and correction to manual downloads, and keep only the post-download comparison as asynchronous observation.

findings.failure_path: The 'uses none' option lets an export run with no template to check against. That undoes line 4's promise that the service 'cannot skip the check by omitting the template'. Any caller can opt out by choosing none.
findings.smallest_fix: Require 'none' to be an explicit, recorded user confirmation bound to the job and data snapshot. Define the checks that still run for it, such as data-snapshot integrity, and make the publish credential record that 'none' was chosen.

findings.failure_path: Admins get a blanket permission to bypass the gate, with no scope, expiry, audit record or link to the credential. Unchecked reports can then be published to the shared folder and sent to subscribers without any trace.
findings.smallest_fix: Limit each override to one job or report family and make it expire. Require a reason, write it to the audit log, and mark the published report and its notifications as overridden.

findings.failure_path: 'If the check is unavailable, report a fault' does not say what happens next. There is no retry, no time limit for the holding area, and no cleanup. It also does not cover the template version or data snapshot changing between confirmation and the check. Jobs could pile up in holding indefinitely, or a stale confirmation could approve a different template version.
findings.smallest_fix: Specify retry with backoff and a limit, a retention period and cleanup for the holding area, and who is alerted. Require the check to fail if the template version or snapshot no longer matches the confirmation.

findings.failure_path: The plan has no tests and no criteria for leaving staging or rolling back. The acceptance criterion 'can be implemented and rolled out safely' therefore has nothing to measure it. Bypasses (manual download, 'none', admin override, credential mismatch, check unavailable shown as a pass) would not be caught before enforcement starts.
findings.smallest_fix: Add tests that fail in each of these cases: a report is published without a matching credential; a 'none' or manual-download path skips the pre-export check; an outage is reported as a pass; a template-version mismatch is accepted. Define staging exit metrics and a rollback switch for each team and report family.

findings.failure_path: 'Template confirmation already exists and is fully rolled out' is stated as an absolute with no evidence behind it. The plan depends on it: line 1 relies on confirmation that binds to the template version, job and snapshot, which may not exist on every export path, manual downloads included.
findings.smallest_fix: Cite evidence such as rollout coverage or the paths where confirmation is enforced, or soften the claim and list binding to template version, job and snapshot as new work.

findings.failure_path: The requester asked for 「导出前自动检查并修正报表模板」, meaning the template is checked and fixed before export. Step 2 instead lets rendering run as today and only checks pages after rendering. Nothing checks or corrects the template before export, so a report that doesn't match the template is still produced, and the main part of the request isn't covered.
findings.smallest_fix: Add a pre-export step that checks the confirmed template version against the data snapshot and fixes the template mapping automatically before rendering starts. The post-render sampling then becomes a secondary check only.

findings.failure_path: The requester said 「导出后的差异只记录下来做观察」: differences found after export should only be recorded. Step 2 turns the post-export check into a blocking gate. Publishing to the shared folder and notifying subscribers both need a matching credential, and unchecked reports are held. This blocks delivery in a way the request rules out.
findings.smallest_fix: Drop the credential gate and the holding area for the post-export check. Publish as today and log the differences found after export for observation.

findings.failure_path: When a difference is found, step 3 has the export service revise the mapping and then wait for the user to reconfirm. That replaces the requested automatic correction with a manual step. Reports wait indefinitely if the user never responds. The revised mapping also changes the template binding, so the credential from step 2 may no longer match the template it was issued for.
findings.smallest_fix: Make the correction automatic and run it before export, without a reconfirmation wait. If a person must review a fix, record that as a separate requirement with a timeout and a defined result when it expires.

findings.failure_path: If the check is unavailable, the plan reports a fault, and unchecked reports stay in the private holding area (line 7). There is no retry, timeout, or release path, so an outage of the checker stops all report publishing for teams where the gate is enforced, with no defined way to recover.
findings.smallest_fix: Once the post-export gate is removed, a checker outage only means missing observation records. Keep a fault alert for the outage, but don't hold reports back.

findings.failure_path: Manual downloads skip the check, so their reports can go out without matching the template. That contradicts the goal that exported reports match the confirmed template, and it is a lasting way around the check.
findings.smallest_fix: Run the pre-export check-and-fix step on manual downloads too. It happens before rendering, so downloads don't need to wait for a post-render result.

findings.failure_path: Users can choose 'uses none' for the template. The plan doesn't say what is checked or fixed in that case, so choosing none may skip the check completely. That undercuts the stated guarantee that the service 'cannot skip the check by omitting the template'.
findings.smallest_fix: Define what happens for 'none': either check against a default rule set, or say plainly that these exports are out of scope and log them.

findings.failure_path: The request doesn't call for the staged rollout (staging, then one team and one report family at a time) or for an admin permission override, because nothing in the request blocks delivery. The override has no audit trail and is a permanent way around the gate.
findings.smallest_fix: Drop the admin override and the per-team, per-report-family enforcement rollout. If a staged rollout is still wanted for the pre-export auto-fix, describe it separately with audit logging.

findings.failure_path: The plan has no tests or acceptance evidence: nothing would show that the pre-export fix happened, that post-export differences were logged without blocking, or how the checker-outage case behaves. So 'can be implemented and rolled out safely' can't be verified.
findings.smallest_fix: Add a verification section with concrete cases: a template mismatch is fixed before export, a post-export difference is logged and the report is still published, a checker outage raises a fault without blocking, and a manual download is checked before export.

findings.failure_path: 'Template confirmation already exists and is fully rolled out' is an absolute claim with no evidence cited. Step 1 also describes new binding to the template version, export job and data snapshot, which may not exist yet, so the claim may overstate what is already built.
findings.smallest_fix: Cite evidence for the rollout claim (coverage or a link), or reword it. Mark the binding in step 1 as new work if it is.

findings.failure_path: The requester asked for an automatic template check and fix before export, with differences found after export only recorded for observation. The plan has no automatic check or fix before export: step 1 is the template confirmation that already exists. Instead, step 2 checks after rendering and turns that check into a blocking gate, with a credential and a private holding area. Template drift is still not corrected before export, and post-export differences now block publishing and subscriber notifications. That contradicts 'only recorded for observation'.
findings.smallest_fix: Add an automatic check-and-correct step that runs before rendering, against the confirmed template version. Make the post-render sampling observe-only: record differences and don't hold reports. Drop the publish credential and the private holding area.

findings.failure_path: When a difference is found, the export service changes the template mapping and waits for the user to reconfirm. That adds a manual step the request didn't ask for, which wanted automatic correction. It also mutates the confirmed template because of a post-export difference that was only supposed to be recorded. This can silently move the template away from what the user confirmed, and it stalls exports until someone acts.
findings.smallest_fix: Do automatic correction only in the pre-export step, and limit it to bringing the export back in line with the confirmed template. Post-export differences should produce a log or observation record and leave the template mapping and the reconfirmation flow alone.

findings.failure_path: Manual downloads skip the check entirely and deliver the report right away. Combined with the admin bypass on line 12, step 1's promise that the export service 'cannot skip the check' is false. Unchecked, possibly template-mismatched reports leave the platform through download while shared publishing is blocked, so the gate gives inconsistent protection.
findings.smallest_fix: Run the same pre-export automatic check and fix on every export path, including manual downloads. After export, only record differences on all paths.

findings.failure_path: The request didn't ask for the staged rollout (staging, then one team and one report family at a time), the enforcement gate or the admin permission to bypass the gate. They add rollout restrictions, a permission surface and an unaudited bypass that the request doesn't need.
findings.smallest_fix: Drop the per-team and per-report-family enforcement and the admin bypass permission. If a rollout step is needed, keep a single observe-first note for the post-export recording.

findings.failure_path: 'If the check is unavailable, report a fault, never a pass' doesn't say what happens to the export. Under step 2 the report sits in the holding area with no timeout, retry or release path. Also, sampling pages can miss field differences, yet a credential is still issued claiming the report matches the template and data snapshot.
findings.smallest_fix: Define how the pre-export check fails: retry, then block the export with a visible fault. State that post-export sampling is partial, and that its output is an observation, not a match guarantee.

findings.failure_path: 'Template confirmation already exists and is fully rolled out' is an absolute claim with no evidence cited, and step 1 depends on it. The plan also has no test or evidence that would fail if template drift got through: no case for a mismatched template, the manual-download path, the admin bypass or an unavailable check.
findings.smallest_fix: Cite evidence for the rollout status, such as a flag state or coverage data, or soften the claim. Add acceptance tests: pre-export correction of a template that has drifted, the same check on manual downloads, and post-export differences being recorded without blocking.

findings.failure_path: The requester asked for an automatic check and fix of the report template before export (「导出前自动检查并修正报表模板」). The plan instead renders first and checks afterwards (step 2). Nothing in the plan checks or fixes the template before rendering, so exports built from a mismatched template still get rendered, and the requested pre-export behavior is never delivered.
findings.smallest_fix: Add a pre-render step that automatically checks the confirmed template against the export's field mapping and fixes it before rendering starts. Make that step the only gate.

findings.failure_path: The requester said post-export differences should only be recorded for observation (「导出后的差异只记录下来做观察」). Step 2 does the opposite: the post-render check blocks publishing to the shared folder and blocks subscriber notification, and unchecked reports sit in a holding area. A sampling miss, a false positive or a check outage would then hold back reports the requester expected to go out.
findings.smallest_fix: Turn the post-export check into log-only observation. Drop the publish credential, the publish/notify block and the private holding area.

findings.failure_path: When the post-export check finds a difference, the export service revises the shared template mapping and waits for the user to reconfirm. This is an automatic change to a shared template driven by an observation-only signal. Other export jobs running on the same template version would pick up the revised mapping mid-flight, and the stated outcome is a user wait loop, not the automatic pre-export fix the requester asked for.
findings.smallest_fix: Remove the post-export mapping revision and the reconfirm wait. Template fixes happen only in the automatic pre-export step; post-export differences are only recorded.

findings.failure_path: Manual downloads skip the check entirely, and their check report arrives after the file has already been delivered. A user can get a report from an unfixed template, which defeats the requested pre-export check and fix.
findings.smallest_fix: Run the pre-export automatic check and fix for manual downloads too. Only the post-export observation may run asynchronously.

findings.failure_path: The request doesn't ask for staged enforcement per team and per report family, or for an admin permission override. Both add mechanisms the requester didn't want. The override is also an unaudited path around the check.
findings.smallest_fix: Drop the per-team/per-family enforcement schedule and the admin bypass permission. If a rollout step is needed, use a single staging observation step for the pre-export fix.

findings.failure_path: Step 1 relies on a manual user confirmation (keep / adapt / none) bound to the template version, export job and data snapshot to stop the check being skipped. The request asks for an automatic check. This binding adds an anti-bypass layer the request doesn't need, and the claim that the export service 'cannot skip the check' is an absolute that nothing in the plan backs up.
findings.smallest_fix: Drop the anti-skip binding and the 'cannot skip' claim. Have the pre-export step run automatically on every export path, and state that coverage as a requirement to be tested.

findings.failure_path: The plan says to 'report a fault, never a pass' when the check is unavailable, but it defines no retry, timeout or recovery. Under the current gating design, a check outage leaves every report stuck in holding with no defined way out.
findings.smallest_fix: Define how the pre-export step behaves on failure: block that export with a visible error and retry. For the post-export observer, an outage should only be logged.

findings.failure_path: The plan gives no test or evidence strategy. It also bases its verification on sampled pages, which can miss differences on the pages it doesn't sample, yet the plan presents a sampled pass as proof the report matches. No test is named that would fail if a mismatched template got through export.
findings.smallest_fix: Add tests that inject a template/field mismatch and assert that the pre-export step fixes it or blocks the export. Describe sampling as observation only, not as proof of a full match.
